summary: Add src/scheduler.ts: a per-service activity ledger (in-memory Map keyed by ServiceKey `<branchRef>/<serviceId>`, persisted to <dataDir>/activity.json on a 5 s debounced flush, never in state.json), a 30 s sweep that copies the cloud's five conditions (running, not alwaysOn, stamp older than the idle window, older than the create grace, no op in flight; sleep-and-wake.md:47-68), memory-pressure eviction of the least-recently-active non-alwaysOn service when /proc/meminfo MemAvailable falls under a 15 % floor or a wake needs room, sleep = `docker stop -t <grace>` (compute 10 s, databases 30 s), and wake = `docker start` + readiness probe (router dial on the app port; `pg_isready` for postgres) behind a per-key singleflight and an op-in-flight set, exposed as engine.wake/engine.sleep/engine.touch. Postgres and managed-DB containers sleep with the same rules (db window 10 min, compute 5 min). Service views gain the cloud's vocabulary: asleep reads as state 'suspended' with desired_state 'running' (insta-compute.ts:1652-1666), runtime-health 'standby', oss runtime 'asleep'; user-stopped is 'stopped' and is never woken by traffic. Implements the cloud's PUT …/always-on (plat server.ts:2167-2188), GET/PUT …/limits (plat server.ts:2003-2063, gated `service.upgrade`) mapped to `--cpus/--memory` via `docker update` on every branch's container plus create-time flags, and PATCH database/settings {scaleToZero, idleTimeout, cpu, memory} for postgres (plat server.ts:2957-2970). New branches come up asleep: compute clones are `docker create`d and never started, pg/managed are provisioned, readied, then stopped, unless alwaysOn. All scheduler I/O goes through a small Runtime seam (DockerRuntime in prod, FakeRuntime in tests) so the contract suite covers every rule without Docker.

src/scheduler.ts types:
  export interface ActivityRecord { createdAt: number; lastActiveAt: number; sleptAt?: number; wokeAt?: number; lastRssBytes?: number; lastSleepReason?: SleepReason }
  export type WakeDoor = 'traffic' | 'api' | 'deploy'
  export type SleepReason = 'idle' | 'memory' | 'branch-create'
  export interface ServiceTarget { key: ServiceKey; kind: ServiceKind; container: string; network: string; port: number; projectId: string; branchId: string; serviceId: string; alwaysOn: boolean; desiredState: 'running'|'stopped'|'suspended'; idleSecs: number; limits?: ServiceLimits; managedType?: ManagedDbType }
  export interface Runtime {
    containers(): Promise<Map<string, 'running'|'paused'|'exited'|'created'|'restarting'|'dead'>>   // docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.State}}' (same read as engine.ts:723)
    stats(): Promise<Map<string, number>>            // docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}}\t{{.MemUsage}}', first half parsed with observe.parseSize (observe.ts:36)
    memory(): { availableBytes: number; totalBytes: number } | null   // /proc/meminfo MemAvailable/MemTotal (host values are visible inside a container); null when absent (macOS)
    start(container: string): Promise<void>          // docker start
    stop(container: string, graceSecs: number): Promise<void>   // docker stop -t <grace>
    unpause(container: string): Promise<void>
    update(container: string, limits: ServiceLimits): Promise<void>   // docker update --cpus <cpu> --memory <mb>m --memory-swap <mb>m
    probe(t: ServiceTarget): Promise<boolean>        // postgres: docker exec pg_isready -U postgres -d app (postgres.ts:39); compute+managed: dial(network, container, port) then destroy the socket. `dial` is injected from the WP2 router (it is the component that can reach containers in both run modes).
  }

  readonly scheduler: Scheduler
  serviceKey(project, branch, serviceId): ServiceKey
  targetOf(key): ServiceTarget | undefined       // resolves ref -> branch by scanning state.branches for b.ref ?? derived ref; maps cp-<g> -> io-<ref>-app-<g>:app.port, pg-db -> io-<ref>-pg:5432, rd-/my-/mo- -> managedContainerName():MANAGED_DB[type].port; fills alwaysOn/desiredState/idleSecs/limits
  serviceTargets(): ServiceTarget[]              // every materialised service on every branch (pg + managed on all branches; compute only where branch.apps[group] exists)

  wake(key, opts: { door: WakeDoor }): Promise<void>        // delegates to scheduler.wake; ROUTER (WP2) calls this with door 'traffic'
  sleep(key, reason): Promise<boolean>

  stateOf(key): 'running'|'asleep'|'stopped'|'paused'|'starting'|'none'   // ROUTER reads this (cached, refreshed every sweep and by every scheduler op) to decide proxy vs hold-and-wake
  withOp<T>(keys: ServiceKey[], fn): Promise<T>              // marks op in flight for the sweep/eviction; used around deploy, lifecycle, restart, branch create/destroy, service add/remove/rename, volume ops, db management
  setAlwaysOn(projectId, serviceId, enabled): Promise<{ service }>
  serviceLimits(projectId, serviceId): { limits, cap, volume? }
  setServiceLimits(projectId, serviceId, { memoryMb, cpu? }): Promise<{ service, limits, cap }>
  private ensurePgAwake(project, branch): Promise<void>      // wake(pgKey, {door:'api'}) before any db.query (callers: dbSetPassword, dbListDatabases, dbCreateDatabase, dbDeleteDatabase, dbExtensions, dbPatchExtensions, dbInsight, dbMetricsSnapshot, dbActivity, dbQueryStats, engine.ts:1067-1267) and before db.cloneInto when WP5 reports the reflink probe failed (pg_basebackup needs a live source)
Hooks in existing methods:
  provisionBranch (engine.ts:66-105): after the Branch row is written, scheduler.register(pgKey), register(managedKeys) with createdAt = now.
  createBranch (engine.ts:128-152): wrap in withOp(all new-branch keys); compute clones call deployAllocatingPort with `startAsleep: true` (a new deploy opt: start:false + scheduler.onAsleep(key,'branch-create')) unless effectiveAlwaysOn; after clone + deploy, for pg and each managed key: if !effectiveAlwaysOn -> sleep(key,'branch-create').
  deployLocked (engine.ts:203-258): pass limits from project.serviceSettings[cp-<g>].limits; after the adapter deploy: if started -> scheduler.onUp(key) (ready stamp, clears sleptAt); if start:false because standing intent stopped -> scheduler.onStopped(key); if startAsleep -> onAsleep. A redeploy of an ASLEEP service starts it (cloud: a deploy on a suspended service brings it up, sleep-and-wake.md:121-123), so the existing `start: standing !== 'stopped'` stays.
  lifecycleLocked (engine.ts:565-584): 'start' -> mutate desiredState 'running' FIRST, then engine.wake(key,{door:'api'}) (replaces the bare compute.start; errors are best-effort like today, state read after); 'stop' -> compute.stop(ref, group, {graceSecs}) then scheduler.onStopped(key); 'suspend' -> compute.suspend then scheduler.onPaused(key).
  liveState (engine.ts:709-711): adapter 'stopped' + scheduler record sleptAt set + desiredState 'running' -> 'suspended'; scheduler wake in flight -> 'suspended' too (cloud row says suspended until the wake lands).
  services() (engine.ts:413-471): drop the `docker ps` read at engine.ts:426; runtime = scheduler.stateOf mapped running->online, asleep->asleep, paused->suspended, stopped->stopped, none->none, starting->online-pending? no: starting->'asleep' (still not serving); add always_on on compute + managed rows.
  runtimeHealth() (engine.ts:718-750): keep the one docker read but overlay: exited + record.sleptAt -> 'standby'; wake in flight -> 'starting'; exited, desired running, no sleptAt -> 'crashed' (unchanged, engine.ts:736).
  dbInstance() (engine.ts:1016-1027): scaleToZero = branch.dbScaleToZero ?? true; idleTimeoutSecs = branch.dbIdleTimeoutSecs ?? cfg.idle.dbSecs.
  dbSettings() (engine.ts:1033-1049): accept scaleToZero (boolean), idleTimeout (int >= 0; 0 = never sleeps this branch's pg, same as the cloud's disabled sweep), cpu/memory quantity strings -> ServiceLimits validated on the same grid -> persist branch.dbLimits and runtime.update(io-<ref>-pg). Events: 'database.settings' with the changed fields (existing kind, engine.ts:1045).
  destroyBranch/destroyProject/removeComputeService/removeManagedService: scheduler.forget(keys) after the containers are gone.
  renameComputeService/renameManagedService: scheduler.rekey(oldKey, newKey) per branch (container names change with docker rename, engine.ts:802,918).
  restartLocked (engine.ts:598-616): unchanged; an asleep service has desired 'running' so restart is allowed and lands running via deployLocked.
Router contract (WP2 must call): on every HTTP request start engine.touch(key) and every 5 s while the handler is in flight; on every non-empty read in a TCP splice, both directions; before proxying: s = engine.stateOf(key); if s === 'running' proxy, else await engine.wake(key,{door:'traffic'}) (bounded by wakeTimeoutSecs, ServiceStoppedError -> 503 'service is stopped' / TCP refuse, WakeTimeoutError -> 503 / reset); on ECONNREFUSED from a 'running' cache entry call wake once (it re-inspects live state) and retry once.
Templates (WP6) must call engine.setAlwaysOn(projectId, `cp-<group>`, true) for manifests with alwaysOn: true (templates/hermes/insta.template.yaml:24) at template-deploy time.

algorithm:
DEFINITIONS
- key = `${branchRef}/${serviceId}`; target = engine.targetOf(key) (container name, kind, network, port, alwaysOn, desiredState, idleSecs, limits).
- kinds and containers: compute cp-<g> -> io-<ref>-app-<g> (compute.ts:4), postgres pg-db -> io-<ref>-pg (postgres.ts:7), managed rd-/my-/mo-<name> -> io-<ref>-<prefix>-<name> (manageddb.ts:100-101).
- idleSecs(target): compute -> cfg.idle.computeSecs; postgres -> branch.dbIdleTimeoutSecs ?? cfg.idle.dbSecs; managed -> cfg.idle.dbSecs. 0 = never swept.
- alwaysOn(target): compute/managed -> project.serviceSettings[sid]?.alwaysOn ?? cfg.alwaysOnDefault (false); postgres -> !(branch.dbScaleToZero ?? true).
- ledger: Map<ServiceKey, ActivityRecord>; dirty flag; flush timer 5 s (unref); flush also on stop(). File <dataDir>/activity.json { version:1, services }, atomic write (tmp + rename).
- opsInFlight: Map<ServiceKey, number> (refcount). wakes: Map<ServiceKey, Promise<void>>. sleeps: Map<ServiceKey, Promise<boolean>>.
- stateCache: Map<container, dockerState> refreshed by every sweep and patched by sleep/wake/onUp/onStopped.

STAMP WRITERS (cloud 1.2, sleep-and-wake.md:23-45)
- touch(key): rec = ledger.get(key) ?? register(key); rec.lastActiveAt = now(); dirty = true. Synchronous, no I/O. The router calls it at HTTP request start and every 5 s while a handler is in flight; on every non-empty read in a TCP splice both directions (the splice stamps once after the upstream dial too). Nothing else stamps: no probes, no docker stats, no outbound.
- onUp(key) (ready stamp, cloud executor row): rec.lastActiveAt = now; delete rec.sleptAt; rec.wokeAt = now; stateCache[container] = 'running'. Called by wake() on success and by deployLocked after a started deploy.
- onAsleep(key, reason): rec.sleptAt = now; rec.lastSleepReason = reason; stateCache = 'created'|'exited'.
- onStopped(key): delete rec.sleptAt (a user stop is not sleep); stateCache = 'exited'.
- onPaused(key): stateCache = 'paused'.
- register(key): if absent -> { createdAt: now, lastActiveAt: now } (a NULL stamp falls back to creation, cloud 1.3 item 3).
- forget(keys), rekey(old,new): move the record, keep timestamps.

BOOT RECONCILE (scheduler.start())
1. Load activity.json (missing/corrupt -> empty ledger, log once).
2. targets = engine.serviceTargets(); containers = runtime.containers().
3. For each target: register(key) if absent (so a daemon restart gives every existing service a full window, like the cloud's ready stamp). If rec.sleptAt is set and the container is running (someone started it by hand, or a redeploy) -> delete sleptAt, stamp now. If the container is exited and rec.sleptAt is unset -> leave it (reads as crashed or stopped, honestly). Drop ledger keys with no target.
4. If runtime.memory() is null log once 'memory-pressure eviction disabled (no /proc/meminfo)'.
5. Ticker: setInterval(sweep, cfg.idle.sweepSecs*1000).unref(); a tick is skipped while the previous sweep is still running (sweeping flag). Immediately run one sweep's pressure pass (a dockerd restart brought every `unless-stopped` container back, possibly over the floor).

SWEEP (every 30 s; cloud 1.3, sleep-and-wake.md:47-68)
1. containers = runtime.containers(); stateCache = containers. rss = runtime.stats() (skipped when no container is running); for each running target rec.lastRssBytes = rss[container] when present.
2. targets = engine.serviceTargets(); now = clock().
3. candidates = targets where ALL hold:
   a. containers.get(container) === 'running'  (paused, created, exited never qualify; the optional pause-then-stop tier is off and out of scope);
   b. !alwaysOn(target);
   c. target.desiredState === 'running' (compute only; pg/managed always 'running');
   d. idleSecs > 0 and now - rec.lastActiveAt >= idleSecs*1000;
   e. now - rec.createdAt >= cfg.idle.createGraceSecs*1000;
   f. opsInFlight.get(key) is falsy, wakes.has(key) false, sleeps.has(key) false.
4. For each candidate (concurrency 4, order oldest stamp first): await sleep(key, 'idle'). Errors are logged and retried next pass (the cloud defers on transient errors).
5. Pressure pass: await evictForRoom(0, new Set()).
6. Persist if dirty.
With a 300 s window and 30 s cadence an idle compute service sleeps 300 to 330 s after its last stamp; databases 600 to 630 s.

SLEEP(key, reason) -> boolean
1. If sleeps.has(key) return that promise. If wakes.has(key) or opsInFlight.get(key) return false (never race a wake or an op; the sweep tries again next pass).
2. target = targetOf(key); if none return false. grace = kind === 'compute' ? cfg.idle.stopGraceSecs : cfg.idle.stopGraceDbSecs.
3. Promise: opsInFlight++ ; state = stateCache or runtime.containers().get(container). If 'paused' -> return false (user pause is intent). If not 'running' -> onAsleep(key, reason) only if state is 'created' (a never-started clone), else return false.
4. await runtime.stop(container, grace)  = `docker stop -t <grace> <container>`. docker sends the image's STOPSIGNAL then SIGKILL after grace: postgres:16-alpine declares STOPSIGNAL SIGINT (fast shutdown), valkey/mysql/mongo take SIGTERM and shut down cleanly; a compute image's own init gets SIGTERM. A stop also clears `--restart unless-stopped`'s auto-restart, so asleep containers stay asleep across a dockerd restart while running ones come back (restart-policy.test.ts rationale).
5. onAsleep(key, reason); emit event source 'resource' kind 'service.sleep' { service: serviceId, branch, reason } (dedup none); return true.
6. finally: opsInFlight--, sleeps.delete(key), mark dirty.
desiredState is NOT touched: the row keeps 'running', which is what makes the service wakeable.

EVICT FOR ROOM(needBytes, exclude)
1. mem = runtime.memory(); if null return (unsupported host). floor = mem.totalBytes * cfg.memory.floorPct/100.
2. loop while (mem.availableBytes - needBytes) < floor:
   a. pool = targets where stateCache running, !alwaysOn, desiredState 'running', !exclude.has(key), no op/wake/sleep in flight.
   b. protected = pool where now - (rec.wokeAt ?? 0) < cfg.idle.wakeProtectSecs*1000; pool = pool minus protected, or protected alone if the rest is empty (anti-thrash: a just-woken service goes last).
   c. if pool empty: log 'memory floor unreachable: N MiB available, floor F MiB, nothing evictable' once per sweep; return.
   d. victim = min by rec.lastActiveAt (oldest first), tie -> larger lastRssBytes.
   e. await sleep(victim.key, 'memory'); mem = runtime.memory() (MemAvailable moves as soon as the cgroup is gone).
Eviction ignores the idle window and the create grace on purpose (pressure is not idleness) but never touches alwaysOn, paused, user-stopped or in-flight services.

WAKE(key, { door })  (cloud 1.5, sleep-and-wake.md:101-128)
1. target = targetOf(key); if none throw NotFound.
2. If door === 'traffic' and target.kind === 'compute' and target.desiredState !== 'running' throw ServiceStoppedError ('service is stopped'). A user-stopped or user-paused service is never woken by traffic; only the start verb (door 'api', which first sets desiredState 'running') or a deploy (door 'deploy') may. pg/managed have no stop verb so this never triggers for them.
3. If wakes.has(key) return the existing promise (singleflight: any number of held connections cost one docker start).
4. Promise (stored in wakes before any await): opsInFlight++;
   a. state = runtime.containers().get(container) (live read, not the cache).
   b. 'running' and !rec.sleptAt: fast path -> if await runtime.probe(target) then touch(key), return; else fall through to the readiness loop (a crashed-and-restarting app).
   c. 'paused': only door 'api' reaches here (step 2) -> runtime.unpause(container); goto readiness.
   d. 'exited' | 'created' | 'dead': need = rec.lastRssBytes ?? (target.limits ? target.limits.memoryMb*1048576 : DEFAULT_RSS[kind]) with DEFAULT_RSS = compute 256 MiB, postgres 128 MiB, managed 256 MiB; await evictForRoom(need, new Set([key])); await runtime.start(container). A start error (image gone, port clash) rejects immediately with its message.
   e. 'restarting': goto readiness.
   f. readiness loop: deadline = now + cfg.idle.wakeTimeoutSecs*1000; every 250 ms: if await runtime.probe(target) break; if runtime.containers().get(container) (re-read every 2 s) is 'exited'|'dead' throw new Error('service exited during wake'); at deadline throw WakeTimeoutError('service did not become ready within 60 s'); the container is left running so the sweep sleeps it after its window and logs can be read.
   g. onUp(key); emit 'service.wake' { service, branch, door, ms }; resolve.
   h. finally: opsInFlight--, wakes.delete(key), dirty.
   probe: postgres -> `docker exec io-<ref>-pg pg_isready -U postgres -d app` exit 0; compute and managed -> dial(network, container, port) connects within 1 s (managed: redis 6379, mysql 3306, mongodb 27017 from MANAGED_DB[type].port).

OP BOOKKEEPING
engine.withOp(keys, fn): for each key opsInFlight++ ; try fn() finally --. Wraps: deployLocked (cp key), lifecycleLocked, restartLocked, createBranch (every key of the new branch plus the source pg key when the reflink probe fails), destroyBranch/destroyProject (all keys), addManagedService/removeManagedService/renameManagedService (their keys on every branch), addComputeService (none), removeComputeService/renameComputeService, setServiceVolume/removeServiceVolume (cp key on each branch), ensurePgAwake callers (pg key for the duration of the db.query), setServiceLimits (all keys touched). The existing per-app serialize() chain (engine.ts:32-37) stays; withOp is the sweep-visible flag, serialize is the mutual exclusion.

NEW BRANCH STARTS ASLEEP (spec §5.6)
In createBranch (engine.ts:128-152) inside withOp:
1. provisionBranch as today (pg + managed come up running; WP5's reflink fork may pass start:false to db.provision when the data dir is pre-populated, then no readiness wait is needed).
2. db.cloneInto / storage.cloneInto as today (WP5 changes the inside).
3. For each source app: deployAllocatingPort(..., { startAsleep: !effectiveAlwaysOn(cp-<g>) }) -> deployLocked passes start:false to compute.deploy (container 'created', zero RAM ever) and calls scheduler.onAsleep(key, 'branch-create'); alwaysOn apps start and get onUp.
4. For pg-db and each managed key: if !effectiveAlwaysOn -> await sleep(key, 'branch-create').
5. Records for the new keys have createdAt = now, so an explicit wake gets the full create grace before the sweep looks at it.
Cost of a new idle branch after this: disk only.

SERVICE VIEW MAPPING (one table, used by services(), serviceState(), runtimeHealth())
docker state | rec.sleptAt | desiredState -> oss runtime | cloud state | runtime-health
running | any | running -> online | running | healthy
running | any | stopped/suspended (transient, mid-op) -> online | running | healthy
paused | - | suspended -> suspended | suspended | standby
exited/created | set | running -> asleep | suspended | standby
exited/created | unset | stopped/suspended -> stopped | stopped | standby
exited/dead | unset | running -> stopped | stopped | crashed
restarting or wake in flight | - | - -> asleep | suspended | starting
no container | - | - -> none | none | none
docker unreadable -> runtime omitted | unknown | unknown

LIMITS
validate(memoryMb, cpu?): cpu = cpu ?? SHARED_CPU_LADDER.find(c => memoryMb <= c*2048) (undefined -> 400 'no vCPU size can carry N MB of memory'); reject cpu not in ladder; memoryMb not integer or % 256; memoryMb outside [256*cpu, 2048*cpu]; per-axis cap check only when raising (cloud services.ts:2182-2188): cpu > 8 or memoryMb > 8192 -> 400. Apply: for every branch container of the service: runtime.update(container, limits) = `docker update --cpus <cpu> --memory <mb>m --memory-swap <mb>m <container>` (memory-swap equal to memory so the ceiling is a ceiling and eviction accounting holds; docker update is legal on created/exited containers too). Count failures; any failure -> 502 with 'applied to k/n', stored value unchanged. Success -> persist project.serviceSettings[sid].limits; deploys/provisions after that add `--cpus`, `--memory`, `--memory-swap` at create. Postgres via PATCH database/settings cpu/memory: parse '2500m' -> ceil(2.5) -> 4 on the ladder? No: cpu quantity -> ceil to the next ladder value; memory '4Gi' -> 4096, '2048Mi' -> 2048, then the same grid; persist branch.dbLimits; update io-<ref>-pg.

ALWAYS-ON
setAlwaysOn(projectId, sid, enabled): serviceOf(sid).type must be compute or managed else 400; persist project.serviceSettings[sid].alwaysOn; emit 'service.alwaysOn'; return { service: row }. No container action (cloud services.ts:1438-1443). Postgres: PATCH database/settings { scaleToZero } persists branch.dbScaleToZero (the CLI's `insta db always-on on` sends scaleToZero:false, cli db.ts:23).

RUNTIME (DockerRuntime, all via src/docker.ts docker())
containers(): docker ps -a --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.State}}' -> Map. stats(): docker stats --no-stream --format '{{.Name}}\t{{.MemUsage}}' -> parseSize(first half) (observe.ts:36,54); a failure returns an empty map. memory(): readFileSync('/proc/meminfo') -> MemAvailable/MemTotal kB * 1024; ENOENT -> null. start/stop/unpause/update as named above. probe: as above; dial injected. Timeouts: every docker call in the scheduler is wrapped in a 20 s timeout (a hung dockerd must not wedge the sweep forever); the sweep skips the tick on timeout.

SHUTDOWN
scheduler.stop(): clearInterval, await in-flight sleeps (not wakes), flush ledger. main.ts wires SIGTERM/SIGINT (the daemon container gets SIGTERM from docker compose).

risks: macOS local mode: /proc/meminfo is absent and Docker Desktop's VM memory is what matters, so memory-pressure eviction is disabled there (idle sleep still works); direct TCP to container IPs does not work from a macOS host, so the compute/managed readiness probe depends entirely on the WP2 dial seam being able to reach containers in local mode.

Postgres stop grace: the spec says 10 s; postgres:16-alpine declares STOPSIGNAL SIGINT (fast shutdown) but a large shared_buffers flush can exceed 10 s, after which docker SIGKILLs and the next wake pays crash recovery. Design uses 30 s for databases; the Docker test asserts a clean shutdown.

docker stats latency grows with container count (about 1 to 2 s for dozens); acceptable at a 30 s cadence but a box with hundreds of running containers should skip stats when nothing is near the floor (not built in v1).
Eviction thrash under sustained pressure between two hot services; mitigated by wakeProtectSecs, not eliminated. alwaysOn is the operator's override.

Router state cache staleness: a container that crashes between sweeps reads 'running' until the router's dial fails; WP2 must fall back to wake() on ECONNREFUSED once, or requests get a bare 502 for up to 30 s.

Idle definition blind spots copied from the cloud (sleep-and-wake.md:151-160): headless agents with outbound-only work sleep after the window; templates must ship alwaysOn (hermes/n8n/openclaw do). Spec Known gaps already lists this.

Default alwaysOn differs from the cloud (oss false, cloud INSTA_COMPUTE_ALWAYS_ON_DEFAULT true since 2026-09-07, plat services.ts:714-721); scripts that create compute without --no-always-on behave differently across targets unless the operator sets INSTA_OSS_ALWAYS_ON_DEFAULT=true.

Unlimited containers when limits are unset: the reported effective ceiling (host size snapped to the grid) is honest but a PUT that lowers it is the first time a cgroup limit exists; an app that needed more than 256 MB and gets `memoryMb: 256` is OOM-killed exactly as on the cloud.
